provenance.basis: Audit topic/section inventory and 125 differential concept reviews; source PDFs and rendered lessons require fresh direct inspection before positive claims.

concept_checklist.title: Functions begin with a domain
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The guide now derives the domain restrictions and distinguishes domain, codomain and range; it also contrasts a relation that is not a function.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: Set notation and operations still need a short, usable bridge. The square-root family is not enough to teach specified versus natural domains or a freely chosen codomain.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Read a function’s shape
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The new text handles domain symmetry, even/odd classification, the stationary but strictly increasing cubic, and a compact function-family catalog.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: A catalog paragraph is not a lesson in recognizing piecewise, rational, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic behavior. The visual should distinguish a formula's apparent symmetry from symmetry of its domain.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Transform and compose
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: Negative scales, the b=0 exception, input/output transformation order and composition-domain restrictions are now explained.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: Four transformations remain compressed into prose. Students need to track an actual point through both input and output operations and compare f∘g with g∘f.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Approach a point
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The guide adds contrasting limit failures, the independence of a point value, and velocity interpretation with units.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: Contrasts in text do not supply the missing linked experience. A student should see the same nearby graph with different point values and independently controlled left/right approaches.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Vertical asymptotes
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: Quantifiers and sign distinctions for infinite limits are stronger; unbounded oscillation is explicitly contrasted with a limit to infinity.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: The height cutoff must not impersonate infinity. Separate the domain-side choice from the threshold M, and provide an example where a zero denominator is removable.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Limit laws and squeezing
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The guide now states law hypotheses and develops cancellation and a squeeze estimate.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: The foundational sin(x)/x limit and rationalization are still not developed enough for the advertised toolkit. Avoid deriving the trig limit using a derivative whose proof depends on that limit.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Make “close” precise
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: Quantifier order, its negation, scratchwork and a nonlinear δ construction are now explicit.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: An automatically displayed admissible δ still does not teach its discovery. The independent practice is easier than the nonlinear reasoning being explained.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Continuity and intermediate values
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: An IVT existence example, a failed-hypothesis contrast and bisection discussion are present; existence is not confused with uniqueness.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: Continuity matching, completeness in the bisection proof, and the role of each endpoint hypothesis need fuller instructional steps.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: From secants to a tangent
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The derivative-at-a-point/function distinction, quadratic calculation and units are expanded; a reciprocal-function definition exercise supplies transfer.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: The original quotient, its simplified expression and its limiting value need simultaneous presentation. The h=0 display must distinguish a limit from evaluation of 0/0.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Where differentiability fails
concept_checklist.current_assessment_from_audit: The guide retains the differentiability-implies-continuity argument and adds corner-focused practice.
concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: Corners, vertical tangents, oscillatory failure, derivative discontinuity and higher derivatives are distinct learning outcomes. The course source explicitly includes higher derivatives; one corner cannot cover them.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

concept_checklist.title: Build derivatives from rules

concept_checklist.remaining_work_from_audit: A complete, domain-aware trigonometric rule table and representative derivations are still needed. Mixed expressions should expose rule selection rather than present an already simplified result.
concept_checklist.note: Audit assertions are review leads, not verified completion.

source_review_notes: The rendered physical pages 1 and 2 are a cover and synopsis; instruction starts on p3.
Page 7 gives a derivative-definition argument only for the stronger local case f(a)=g(a)=0, continuous derivatives, and g'(a)≠0; it is not the proof of the full L’Hôpital theorem.
On p14, rendered inspection confirms the numerator derivative is 4 cos(4x)/(1+sin(4x)) and the denominator derivative is sec²x; extracted text is unreliable here.
Page 15 states Cauchy’s mean value theorem and proves it with an auxiliary function and Rolle’s theorem.
